title: The gray digest
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The gray digest. Ten cents a page, forty pages, four dollars in dimes from the box in the drawer. The cover is the copier itself. It comes out as a gray square. That's right.

panels.composition: A drawer at home: a cigar box of dimes. A hand counting forty.

image.prompt: close on a hand counting dimes out of a cigar box in a desk drawer, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat copier. WOOD stapling gray sheets at the folding table. The LAUNDRY owner pretending not to watch.

image.prompt: a young man stapling gray photocopied sheets at a laundromat folding table while the owner pretends not to watch, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The cover: the copier, drawn. Copied. A gray square with a coin slot.

image.prompt: close on a gray photocopied booklet cover showing a scratched copier as a gray square with a coin slot, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The rack. The gray digest in it beside last week's black one. Lighter. Wood looking at the two. Winter's the gray one.

image.prompt: a wire rack holding a crisp black-and-white booklet beside a faded gray one, a young man looking at both, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Four dollars in dimes. The cover is the copier. Winter is the gray one.
